name: Clickable view cube in the viewport corner
body: A small cube in the viewport's top-right corner that turns with the camera. Clicking a face applies that face's camera preset, so the view snaps to look at it. It's the same as View > Camera presets, one click away.
plan:
- `engine/src/editor/ViewCube.nox`: the cube's layout and hit test, as pure functions of the orbit camera and the viewport size.
  - Each face's outward normal is projected with only the camera's rotation (orthographic), into a square in the top-right corner.
  - A face is visible when it points at the camera. Visible faces of a cube never overlap, so a hit test takes the first visible face that contains the point.
  - Each face is named after the preset that puts the camera on its side: +Z front, -Z back, +X left, -X right, +Y top, -Y bottom, as `OrbitCamera.ApplyPreset` already defines them.
- Drawing: `BuildViewport` draws the visible faces into the render world's 2D overlay, shaded by how directly they face the camera, with a darker border and the hovered face highlighted. Labels use the font atlas, which `ViewportResources` gains as `FontTexture`.
- Input: the session tracks the hovered face. A left click on a face applies its preset and starts no drag; a press elsewhere is unchanged.
- Tests: `tests/editor` programs for the layout, the hit test, hover and click through the session. The C API test checks that a click in the corner changes the camera.
- Screenshot of the editor with the cube, posted to the chat.

acceptance_criteria.text: The cube turns with the camera and shows each visible face's label
Clicking a face applies its camera preset, and the status line says which
Hovering a face highlights it and doesn't hover the entity behind it
